sources.title: Fictional Nacre preview release notes
sources.text: Nacre released its fictional desktop search preview on September 18, 2026. The preview builds an index of text files in a folder selected by the user. It searches that local index rather than the whole internet. The index is stored on the same computer. This preview has no upload function and sends neither the selected files nor the index to a server. A file outside the selected folder is outside this search index. After editing files, the user must press Rebuild to refresh the index. Until then, a search may return an older passage. Local storage does not guarantee that search results reflect the latest edits. The preview supports plain text files only, not PDFs. It does not understand every document format. Its useful boundary is a searchable copy of a chosen folder, not an automatic answer engine.

sentences.text: Nacre’s fictional desktop preview searches text files inside a folder you choose.
It builds an index on your computer, and this preview sends neither that index nor your files to a server.
But keeping data nearby does not make the index current.
Edit a file, and you still need to press Rebuild before the search reflects that change.
Skip that step, and an old passage can show up instead.
There is another boundary: the preview handles plain text, not PDFs.
So picture a searchable copy of one folder, with a refresh button you control.
The useful distinction is where your data lives versus when your search last caught up.
